N_k^{(0)}.title: Pilot category count
N_k^{(0)}.body: With the pilot-split cell counts \(N^{(0)}_{aky}\) of \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, define the pilot category count \(N_k^{(0)}=\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}N^{(0)}_{aky}\).

m_0.title: Pilot split size \(m_0\)
m_0.body: We write \(m_0:=|I_0|\) for the cardinality of the deterministic pilot split \(I_0\).

T_M.title: Chebyshev polynomial \(T_M\)
T_M.body: For \(M\in\mathbb N\), \(T_M\) denotes the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind, characterized by \(T_M(\cos\theta)=\cos(M\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\).

(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}.title: Falling factorial split-cell count
(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}.body: For a split-one cell count \(N^{(1)}_{aky}\) and multi-index coordinate \(r_{ay}\in\mathbb N_0\), we write \((N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}\) for the falling factorial \(N^{(1)}_{aky}(N^{(1)}_{aky}-1)\cdots(N^{(1)}_{aky}-r_{ay}+1)\) when \(r_{ay}\ge1\), with \((N^{(1)}_{aky})_0=1\).

u^r.title: Four-cell monomial $u^r$
u^r.body: For a four-cell vector \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\) and a multi-index \(r=(r_{ay})_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}\in\mathbb N_0^4\), write \(u^r=\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}u_{ay}^{r_{ay}}\).

A.title: Binary observed treatment $A$
A.body: We write $A\in\{0,1\}$ for the binary observed treatment, with $A=1$ denoting treated status and $A=0$ denoting untreated status.

Y.title: Binary observed outcome $Y$
Y.body: We say \(Y\) is the observed outcome when \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) is the binary outcome coordinate of a single observed unit drawn from the observed-data law \(P\).

Y(•).title: Control potential outcome $Y(0)$
Y(•).body: We say \(Y(0)\) is the control potential outcome when \(Y(0)\) is a \(\{0,1\}\)-valued random variable on the same probability space as \((X,A,Y)\) whose value is the outcome under treatment level \(0\).

\\widehat\\tau_{\\mathrm{ctr}}.title: Centered endpoint estimator $\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}$
\\widehat\\tau_{\\mathrm{ctr}}.body: For \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and observed units \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the centered endpoint estimator by \[ \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n 2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right). \]

\\mu_n.title: Sample law \(\mu_n\)
\\mu_n.body: For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), we write \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law of the observed sample.

\\mu_{02}.title: Control outcome regression \(\mu_{02}\)
\\mu_{02}.body: For an observed-data law \(P\) with \(P(A=0,X=2)>0\), define \(\mu_{02}:=E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=2]\).

\\mu_{11}.title: Treated outcome regression in category 1
\\mu_{11}.body: We write \(\mu_{11}\) for the conditional mean \(E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=1]\), whenever \(P(A=1,X=1)>0\).

\\mu_{12}.title: Treated outcome regression in category 2
\\mu_{12}.body: In the two-category witness, \(\mu_{12}\) is the treated outcome regression in the second covariate category, \(\mu_{12}=E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=2]\), and this construction sets \(\mu_{12}=0\).

g_{M,j}.title: Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients \(g_{M,j}\)
g_{M,j}.body: For an integer \(M\ge2\), we say \(g_{M,j}\), \(0\le j\le M-2\), are the Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients when they are the unique real coefficients satisfying \[\frac{1-\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2x}}{x}=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}g_{M,j}x^j,\] with the left-hand side interpreted by polynomial continuation at \(x=0\), where \(T_M\) is the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.

\\bar\u0001P_k.title: Sparse factorial-polynomial mean \(\bar P_k\)
\\bar\u0001P_k.body: Given a law \(P\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), a degree \(M\), and a scale \(B\), define the sparse factorial-polynomial mean of category \(k\) by \(\bar P_k=P_{M,B}(q_k)\), where \(q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1})\) is the four-cell mass vector for category \(k\) under \(P\).

N_{ak1}.title: Treatment-arm outcome count \(N_{ak1}\)
N_{ak1}.body: For a finite index set \(I\) and observations \((O_i)_{i\in I}\) with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), we write \(N_{ak1}=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,\ X_i=k,\ Y_i=1\}\) for the number of observations in treatment arm \(a\), category \(k\), and outcome level one.

b_0.title: Calibration constant $b_0$
b_0.body: The calibration constant $b_0$ is the fixed numerical value $4096$.

\\alpha_0.title: Hybrid degree constant $\alpha_0$
\\alpha_0.body: The numerical hybrid degree constant is \(\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{32\log 6},\frac{1}{2048\log(27/4)}\right\}\).

\\widehat\u0001P_k.title: Factorial-moment contribution \(\widehat P_k\)
\\widehat\u0001P_k.body:
For \(n\ge N_0\), set \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\). If the ratio-polynomial has monomial expansion
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r,
\]
then the factorial-moment polynomial contribution for category \(k\) is
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}.
\]

M(•).title: Degree schedule \(M(n)\)
M(•).body:
For \(n\ge2\), the logarithmic polynomial degree schedule is
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0\log(en)\rfloor\},
\]
where
\[
\alpha_0
=
\min\left\{
1,\frac{1}{32\log 6},\frac{1}{256\cdot 8\log(27/4)}
\right\}.
\]

c_r.title: Coefficients \(c_r\)
c_r.body:
For a nonnegative integer \(M\) and scale \(B>0\), \(c_r\) is the coefficient of \(u^r\) in the monomial expansion of the ratio-polynomial \(P_{M,B}\):
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M} c_r u^r .
\]

(m_1)_{|r|}.title: Split-size falling factorial \((m_1)_{|r|}\)
(m_1)_{|r|}.body: For the estimation-split size \(m_1\) and four-cell multi-index \(r\), the denominator \((m_1)_{|r|}\) denotes the falling factorial \(\prod_{\ell=0}^{|r|-1}(m_1-\ell)\), with the empty product equal to \(1\).

P^{\\otimes\u0001J}.title: Finite-index product law $P^{\otimes J}$
P^{\\otimes\u0001J}.body: For a finite index set $J$ and a probability law $P$ for one observed unit $O=(X,A,Y)$, we write $P^{\otimes J}$ for the product law on families $(O_j)_{j\in J}$ under which the coordinates are independent and each coordinate has law $P$.

\\le\\ne.title: Euler factor \(\mathrm e\)
\\le\\ne.body: We write \(\mathrm e=\exp(1)\) for the base of the natural logarithm.

N_k.title: Category count \(N_k\)
N_k.body: For a sample \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in I\), indexed by a finite set \(I\), the category count for \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) is \(N_k=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\}\).

N_{ak}.title: Arm-specific category count $N_{ak}$
N_{ak}.body: For observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) indexed by a finite set \(I\), category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\).

B(•).title: Light-cell approximation scale $B(n)$
B(•).body: For the calibrated hybrid estimator, the light-cell approximation scale is \(B(n)=b_0L/m_1\), with \(L=\log(en)\), \(m_1=|I_1|\), and \(b_0=4096\).

N_0.title: Numerical cutoff $N_0$
N_0.body: We define $N_0$ to be the least $N\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $n\ge N$, with $L=\log(en)$, $m_1=|I_1|$, $M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\}$, and $B(n)=b_0L/m_1$, the inequalities $\alpha_0L\ge2$, $4M(n)^2\le m_1$, and $4M(n)/m_1\le3B(n)/4$ all hold.
